cards.explanation: The answer is that the mountain will be raised above the hills. In the last days the mountain of the house of the LORD "…will be established as the chief of the mountains; it will be raised above the hills…" (Micah 4:1). The mountain gets lifted up, friends. That's the picture Micah gives.

The answer is that He will teach them His ways. The nations say, "He will teach us His ways, so that we may walk in His paths." (Micah 4:2). They want to learn, friends. I respect that, because I'm still learning things in my own bakery.

The word is plowshares. "Then they will beat their swords into plowshares…" (Micah 4:3). A plowshare is the blade of a plow, so a weapon becomes a farming tool. Same metal, brand new job. I know a little about that, friends.

The answer is False. Micah says, "Nation will no longer take up the sword against nation, nor will they train anymore for war." (Micah 4:3). Nations won't take up the sword against each other, and they won't train for war. That's a whole lot of retired war gear.

The answer is anyone to frighten him. Each man sits under his own vine and fig tree, "…with no one to frighten him." (Micah 4:4). I spent years in the dark listening for the drawer to open, so I know a calm seat is a gift, friends.

The answer is that they will walk in His name forever. Micah says, "Though all the nations may walk in the name of their gods, yet we will walk in the name of the LORD our God forever and ever." (Micah 4:5). Other crowds go their own ways, but this "we" stays put. Forever and ever is a long time to be faithful, friends.

The word is outcast. The LORD says, "I will gather the lame; I will assemble the outcast…" (Micah 4:6). Those are the folks He's picking up on that day. I've been in the back of a drawer, so that hits home for me, friends.

The word is strong. The LORD says, "…I will make the lame into a remnant, the outcast into a strong nation." (Micah 4:7). The ones on the edge become a strong nation. I once got picked out of a drawer for a big job, so I love hearing it, friends.

The answer is True. The verse says, "Then the LORD will rule over them in Mount Zion from that day and forever." (Micah 4:7). His rule is from that day and forever, friends. That's a ruler worth sticking with.
The word is restored! The LORD says, "…the former dominion will be restored to you…" (Micah 4:8). Something that was lost comes back. I know that feeling, friends, and it is a good one.
